0.long_answer: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), particularly the familial form, is an inherited heart condition characterized by thickening of the heart muscle, most notably in the left ventricle. This disorder is typically inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern and has been strongly associated with mutations in the β-myosin heavy chain gene located on chromosome 14. One common clinical manifestation of HCM is shortness of breath (dyspnea), a term that the American Thoracic Society defines as a 'subjective experience of breathing discomfort'. Thus, patients with HCM may experience this sensation due to the decreased efficiency of the cardiac function and increased cardiac workload associated with the disease.
